question: Which part of seeds forms root on germination?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Radicle**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The radicle is the first part of a seedling to emerge from the seed during the process of germination.
 
• It develops into the primary root, anchoring the plant and absorbing water and nutrients from the soil.
 
• The radicle grows downward, exhibiting positive geotropism, which means it grows in the direction of gravitational pull.
 
• The health and vigor of the radicle are crucial for the establishment and growth of the seedling.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Epicotyl:**

 
 
• বীজপত্রাধিকাণ্ডIt is responsible for the shoot growth and eventually forms the stem and leaves.
 
 
 
• **Plumule:**
 
 
• The plumule is the part of the seed embryo that develops into the shoot bearing the first true leaves of a plant.
 
• It grows upwards, exhibiting negative geotropism, growing away from the gravitational pull.
 
 
 
• **Cotyledon:**
 
 
• Cotyledons are the seed leaves present in the embryo of a seed.
 
• They provide nutrients to the seedling during its initial stages of growth before true leaves develop and photosynthesis begins.
